slot.brief: Compare two octahedral complexes with given ligands from spectrochemical series and identify which is high spin/paramagnetic with justification via t2g-eg filling.

stem: For the octahedral complexes $[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ and $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$, which comparison is correct?
options: $[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ is high-spin and paramagnetic ($t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$); $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ is low-spin and diamagnetic ($t_{2g}^{6}$).
$[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}$ is low-spin and diamagnetic ($t_{2g}^{6}$); $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ is high-spin and paramagnetic ($t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$).

verdicts.working: Fe is +2 in both complexes, so it is d⁶. Weak-field F⁻ gives high-spin t₂g⁴e_g²; strong-field CN⁻ gives low-spin t₂g⁶.

working:
Fe is in the $+2$ oxidation state in both complexes; $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $d^6$.\n$\text{F}^-$ is weak-field: $t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$, with unpaired electrons.\n$\text{CN}^-$ is strong-field: $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$, with no unpaired electrons.

Independent check: Fe is +2 in both complexes, so it is d⁶. Weak-field F⁻ gives high-spin t₂g⁴e_g²; strong-field CN⁻ gives low-spin t₂g⁶.
solution:
In both complexes, Fe is in the $+2$ oxidation state, so Fe$^{2+}$ is $d^6$. F$^-$ is a weak-field ligand, while CN$^-$ is a strong-field ligand.
$$[\text{FeF}_6]^{4-}:\ t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}\ (\text{high-spin, paramagnetic});\quad [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}:\ t_{2g}^{6}\ (\text{low-spin, diamagnetic})$$
